notes: Pinned benchmark slices for LARA. A 'slice' is a named, reproducible set of task IDs + parameters. The autonomous loop references slices by name so that runs from different sessions are directly comparable; raw 'benchmark.py --app venmo --n 5' is not stable because the underlying keyword filter can drift. Update task_ids only when you deliberately want to expand or reshape a slice (record why in 'change_log'). NOTE: the per-app slices below (splitwise-8, todoist-8) ship with empty task_ids because the AppWorld task payloads (data/tasks/*/specs.json) are not installed in every environment. Populate them once, from the LARA dir with the appworld data present, via:  python -c "from benchmark import find_tasks_by_app; print(find_tasks_by_app('splitwise'))"  and paste the first N IDs.

broad-20.purpose: Primary north-star A/B slice. The first 20 train tasks (identical to `benchmark.py --n 20 --dataset train`) — a mixed, positionally-stable sample across apps. Use this to track progress toward the 50% goal (~10/20 correct). Larger than the 5-task smoke slice so model/prompt A/Bs are less positionally noisy.

change_log.note: Initial pin. First 20 train IDs — same set as the benchmark.py default, so parsed panel is directly comparable to the official scorer.

venmo-smoke-5.purpose: Fast iteration on venmo + phone failures. First 5 of the 21 venmo-tagged train tasks; covers the 2a163ab (like-roommates social feed) and afc0fce (comment+like coworker payments) families that dominate today's failure analysis.

change_log.note: Initial pin. Same 5 IDs used across runs ba1uv9gmu / bg22f2uo7 / bv1ew2sc3.
params updated to gpt-4.1-mini + max_iterations=6 to match the new config.py defaults (params are documentation-only; the runtime reads config.py).

Holding app-count constant separates task COMPLEXITY (solution length, API-call volume) from the multi-app COORDINATION gap that dominates the unrestricted difficulty signal. Compare across the three difficulty*-single-20 slices.
